newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Parkway shareholder may sell 14 pct stake.
newsitem.headline: Parkway shareholder may sell 14 pct stake.

text.p: A major shareholder in Parkway Holdings may consider selling its 14 percent stake to DBS Land, a Straits Times report said on Tuesday.

The Ang family of the Petaling Garden group, which owns 42.29 million Parkway shares, was quoted as saying it had not been approached by DBS Land but would consider selling if offered the right price.
The Tan family, another major stakeholder with 21 percent of Parkway's equity, have the first right of refusal, giving them priority to buy the Ang family shares, the newspaper said.
It said it was understood DBS Land had talked with the Ho family of Keck Seng Group to buy its 3.5 percet stake in Parkway, although no deal had been sealed.
The three families are among Parkway's founding members and for years have been warding off potential takeovers with their combined shareholding of nearly 40 percent, it said.
DBS Land bought a 19.16 percent share in Parkway last month. Later, it disclosed some interest in increasing its equity but said the company was not in a hurry.
